recent.narrative: Zarembo Island RAWS measured a peak gust of 55 mph at 1255pm AKDT. The burst of high winds then tracked northward across Sumner Strait and through Wrangell Narrows.

Marine Exchange wind sensors showed a sudden wind shift to the south associated with a squall line at Midway Island starting at 212pm AKDT on the 16th. These winds progressed northward with a peak gust of 50.1 knots measured at Grave Point at 245pm. The sudden wind shift caused this data to be automatically QC'd out, but was later recovered from the source agency. As the squall line reached the Port of Juneau shortly after 3pm, a cruise ship at the AJ Dock was pushed away from the shore causing the lines to snap and the ship to drift out into Gastineau Channel. The NOS Juneau Tide Gauge at the USCG dock measured a peak gust of 47mph at 306pm AKDT.

Marine Exchange of Alaska station at Marmion Island measured a peak gust of 33.6kt at 115pm Tuesday with a sudden wind shift to the south, the same time that the first lightning strikes were detected nearby. As the cell tracked northward the gusts and the wind shift tracked with it. The Juneau airport measured a peak gust of 39kt at 150pm and the ferry M/V Kennicott measured a peak gust of 38kt at 238pm while transiting Favorite Channel.

The burst of high winds tracked northward from the Cape Fanshaw area, up Stephens Passage, and through Gastineau Channel. The FAA webcam at Grave Point, a little more than half way up the channel, measured a max sustained wind of 53 mph at 320pm AKDT (site does not measure gusts) and Point Arden saw a peak of 72 mph. This was followed by the AML Dock along Gastineau Channel in Juneau seeing a peak gust of 60 mph at 432pm and the airport, which includes a seaplane dock, seeing a peak gust of 71mph in the same hour. All of these locations observed these peak gusts after a sudden shift to the south from a light northerly.

Marine Exchange wind sensor at Eldred Rock showed a sudden wind increase out of the south associated with a squall line. The peak gust of 56.3 knots was measured at 424pm AKDT. These winds progressed northward through Lynn Canal, reaching the Skagway Dock at 515pm with a gust of 45.2 knots. The sudden wind change caused some of the data to be automatically QC'd out, but was later recovered from the source agency. Other wind sensors on Eldred Rock showed similar high winds.

The burst of high winds tracked northward from the Juneau to Icy Strait area, and up through Lynn Canal. Winds peaked at 53 mph at Rocky Island and 51 mph at Little Island, then topping out at 59 mph at Eldred Rock. More impactful would have been that all of the observation points noted the peak gusts after a sudden shift to the south from a light northerly.

The burst of high winds tracked northward from the Petersburg area and across Frederick Sound. The FAA webcam at Cape Fanshaw measured a max sustained wind of 42 mph at 230pm AKDT (site does not measure gusts).

Marine Exchange wind sensor at Naked Island showed a sudden wind shift from north to the south associated with a squall line. The peak gust of 52mph was measured at 252pm AKDT. These winds progressed northward through Lynn Canal with the Little Island sensor measuring a peak gust of 39mph at 402pm.

The ferry M/V Kennicott measured a peak gust of 38kt at 238pm shortly after it exited Southern Lynn Canal and the storm was tracking northward into Southern Lynn Canal. Wind gusts estimated based on several continued lightning strikes with the cell and subsequent webcam imagery of a shelf cloud at the leading edge of the wind shift after it moved into Northern Lynn Canal.

recent.area: CAPE DECISION TO CAPE EDGECUMBE OUT TO 15 NM
recent.narrative: The Cape Edgecumbe buoy (46084) measured gusts in excess of 60mph for approximately an hour on the morning of the 26th, including a peak gust of 64mph at 1150am AKDT. In the same hour, a spotter in Sitka reported water spouts just off the coast out to Old Sitka Rocks. The water spouts were not confirmed.

Marine Exchange wind sensor at Rocky Island, at the intersection of Icy Strait, Chatham Strait, and Southern Lynn Canal, showed a sudden wind shift from strong northerly to the south associated with a squall line. The peak gust of 49mph was measured at 317pm AKDT. The Sisters Island NWS sensor measured a peak gust of 47mph in the same hour. These winds progressed northward into Lynn Canal. The sudden wind shift caused some of the data to be automatically QC'd out, but was later recovered from the source agency.
